newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Bahrainis held in Kuwait yet to see lawyers-MP.
newsitem.headline: Bahrainis held in Kuwait yet to see lawyers-MP.

text.p: A Kuwaiti parliamentarian on Tuesday accused the government of preventing defence lawyers from seeing Bahrainis held for allegedly planning sabotage against a Gulf state.
"Until yesterday they did not allow lawyers or families to visit them," Adnan Abdul-Samad, a Moslem Shi'ite Islamist MP, told reporters. "We demand that legal guarantees are provided for them."

Kuwaiti officials have said a non-Kuwaiti Arab group was arrested on March 26 for planning sabotage against a fellow Gulf Arab state. Samad called them Bahrainis. A Bahrain opposition group and media reports had said those arrested included 11 Bahraini Shi'ites.
"If they were charged with real charges they should face Kuwaiti law on Kuwaiti soil," said Samad. He said extraditing them to Bahrain or a third country would violate Kuwaiti laws.
Samad criticised the Interior Ministry for failing to give a detailed statement on the charges and the detainees.

Members of Bahrain's majority Shi'ite community have waged sporadic protests, bombings and arson attacks since Decemeber 1994 to press for political and economic reforms by the Sunni-led government. Almost a third of the 720,000 Kuwaitis are Shi'ites.
